# gitrid

> A bash script that deletes LOCAL git branches in bulk: by name pattern, by "merged into main", or by "upstream branch gone". Describes gitrid 3.1.0 (`gitrid --version`). This file is the reference for AI agents and scripts; `README.md` is the human guide. `gitrid --help` prints a short version of the same rules.

## What it does and does not do

- Deletes local branches only, with `git branch -D`. It never deletes or changes a remote branch, never fetches, never pushes and never switches branch.
- Run it inside the repository to tidy. Outside one it exits `1`.
- Never deleted: the current branch (skipped with a message), and branches named exactly `main` (or `master` when there is no local `main`), `dev`, `develop`, `development`. Matching is on the whole name: `feature/device-list` is not protected.
- Deleting is permanent as far as gitrid goes (the commits can still be found with `git reflog` for a while). A branch without `--merged` is deleted whether its work is merged or not.

## The safe way to run it (agents and scripts)

1. `git fetch --prune` so that "merged" and "gone" are judged from the remote's current state. gitrid does not fetch.
2. Preview with `--dry-run`: the list that would be deleted is printed and nothing is asked or deleted.
3. Show the list to the user and get their agreement.
4. Run the same command with `--yes` in place of `--dry-run`.

```bash
git fetch --prune
gitrid --merged --dry-run     # exit 0: branches listed; exit 2: nothing to delete
gitrid --merged --yes
```

Without `--yes` gitrid asks "Are you sure? (y/n)" on stdin. With no terminal and nothing piped in, it deletes nothing, prints an error to stderr and exits `1`. Do not answer the prompt by piping `y` in: use `--yes`.

## Commands

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `gitrid <pattern>` | Delete branches whose name matches `<pattern>`, merged or not |
| `gitrid --merged [<pattern>]`, `-m` | Only branches fully merged into local `main` or `origin/main` |
| `gitrid --gone [<pattern>]`, `-g` | Only branches whose upstream branch was deleted on the remote |
| `gitrid --nuke` | Every branch that is not protected. With `--merged` or `--gone`: every branch that passes them |
| `--dry-run`, `-n` | With any of the above: list what would be deleted, then stop |
| `--yes`, `-y` | With any of the above: delete without asking |
| `gitrid --list`, `-l` | List every local branch with its status. Read-only |
| `gitrid --list --porcelain` | The same list in a fixed format for a program to read |
| `gitrid --version` | `gitrid version 3.1.0` |
| `gitrid --help`, `-h` | Usage |

- Options can come before or after the pattern. An option that is not listed is an error (exit `1`).
- `<pattern>` is an extended regular expression (`grep -E`) matched anywhere in the branch name. It is not a glob: use `feature/`, not `feature/*`; anchor with `^fix/` or `-123$`. Quote it in the shell.
- With `--merged` or `--gone` the pattern is optional; left out, every branch that passes is taken. With neither, a pattern (or `--nuke`) is required.
- `--merged` and `--gone` together: a branch must pass both.

## How "merged" and "gone" are decided

- **merged**: every commit of the branch is in the local default branch or in `origin/<default>` as last fetched. A branch just created from main with no commits of its own counts as merged. A squash-merged or rebase-merged branch does NOT count: its commits are not in main, only their changes are.
- **gone**: the branch has an upstream configured and that remote branch no longer exists (`git branch -vv` shows `: gone]`). Git learns this only from `git fetch --prune`. This is how to find squash-merged branches whose remote branch was deleted on merge. It says nothing about whether the work was merged: a remote branch deleted for any other reason looks the same. A branch that never had an upstream is never "gone".
- The remote is assumed to be named `origin`.

## Reading the list

`gitrid --list --porcelain` prints one line per local branch, no header, no colours, four tab-separated fields:

```
status<TAB>branch<TAB>commits-on-no-remote<TAB>upstream
```

```
protected	main	0	tracked
merged	feat/login	0	tracked
unmerged	feat/payment	2	none
unmerged	feat/search	1	gone
```

- `status`: `protected`, `merged` or `unmerged` (as defined above).
- `commits-on-no-remote`: how many commits of the branch are on no remote-tracking branch and not in the local default branch. `0` means deleting the branch loses nothing. Above `0` means deleting it loses those commits, with one exception: a `gone` branch that was squash-merged shows its commits here although their changes are in main.
- `upstream`: `tracked` (has an upstream that exists), `gone` (its upstream was deleted on the remote) or `none` (never pushed with an upstream).

Without `--porcelain` the list is for people: colours in a terminal, otherwise lines such as `[UNMERGED] feat/search (1 commit on no remote, upstream gone)`. Parse the porcelain form, not this one.

A deletion or dry run prints the branches indented by two spaces, each followed by `(N commits on no remote)` when N is above 0, and a `WARNING:` line if any branch has such commits. Treat that warning as a reason to stop and ask the user.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Branches were deleted, or a dry run, list, help or version was shown |
| `1` | Error: unknown option, no pattern, not a git repository, no answer to the prompt, or git could not delete a branch. The message is on stderr |
| `2` | No branch matched, so there was nothing to delete (also from a dry run) |
| `3` | The user answered the prompt with anything but `y`/`Y` |

## Recipes

After pull requests were merged with merge commits:

```bash
git fetch --prune && gitrid --merged --dry-run
```

After pull requests were squash-merged and their remote branches deleted:

```bash
git fetch --prune && gitrid --gone --dry-run
```

Only one kind of branch: `gitrid --merged '^feat/' --dry-run`.

Branches that are safe to delete, read from the list: `status` is `merged`, or field 3 is `0`.

```bash
gitrid --list --porcelain | awk -F'\t' '$1 != "protected" && ($1 == "merged" || $3 == 0) { print $2 }'
```

## Do not

- Do not run `gitrid <pattern>` or `gitrid --nuke` without `--merged` unless the user asked to delete unmerged branches: they delete work that exists nowhere else. Always `--dry-run` first and read the `commits on no remote` counts.
- Do not treat `--gone` as proof of a merge. Check the pull request, or the count, when it matters.
- Do not expect remote branches to be removed.

## Installed copies

On Windows the PowerShell command is a batch file that runs the script in WSL (`wsl /usr/local/bin/gitrid.sh`); Git Bash uses an alias to `~/Scripts/gitrid.sh`, and aliases are not loaded in a non-interactive shell, so a script there calls `~/Scripts/gitrid.sh` by path. Linux, macOS and WSL use `/usr/local/bin/gitrid.sh`. The copies are updated separately, by rerunning the setup script for each.
